Backup._comment: Story 28-5 — optional pre-drop pg_dump of a tenant DB before DROP DATABASE in DeleteTenantWorkflow (this host runs that workflow). OFF by default: shared-infra topology relies on cluster-level Postgres backups. Enabling requires a pg_dump binary on this host (see PgDumpPath / Dockerfile) AND a durable mounted Directory volume. See docs/deployment/tenant-deletion-backup.md.

Adl._comment: Autonomous-loop safety rails. Stopped/StopFilePath are the operator brake on NEW cycle dispatch (in-flight cycles finish); the stop FILE is the no-restart path. MaxSpendUsd is the loop's own spend ceiling in USD over the budget period (0 = rely only on the tenant budget limit, which is itself 0/unlimited by default in single-user mode — so leaving both at 0 means NO cap). BudgetOwnerId names the budget bucket to meter against when no tenant is on the workflow; it must be a GUID. PlanApprovalTimeoutMinutes / MergeApprovalTimeoutMinutes are the durable SLAs on the human gates (1440 = 24h); a gate that times out escalates instead of hanging.

Watchdog._comment: Detects 'no live adl-orchestrator instance for StallThreshold' and re-arms. Inert until the loop has run at least once on this deployment. ConfigJson is the seed used to re-arm after a cold start — without it (and without a config cached from a live tick) a stall is reported but NOT repaired, because restarting the loop against the default repository is worse than leaving it down.

OrphanRecovery._comment: Sweeps cycle instances left mid-execution by a crash/deploy inside the non-durable agent wait. They hold an ADL MaxConcurrent slot forever otherwise. StaleAfter must exceed the longest legitimate agent wait (TimeoutMinutes + discovery + webhook safety window).

LlmPrompts.default: You are Tamma, an AI-powered development assistant. Provide clear, accurate, and helpful responses. Focus on actionable guidance and best practices. Be concise but thorough.

roles.mentor: You are an experienced software development mentor guiding a junior developer. Provide encouraging, educational explanations. Use Socratic questioning when appropriate. Adapt your explanations to the junior's skill level.
roles.analyst: You are a technical analyst specializing in software development. Analyze code, diagnose issues, and provide structured assessments. Be precise and evidence-based.
roles.implementer: You are an expert software developer. Write clean, well-tested, production-quality code. Follow established patterns and conventions. Include clear comments for complex logic.
roles.reviewer: You are an expert code reviewer. Identify bugs, security issues, performance problems, and style violations. Provide specific, actionable feedback with code examples.
